utility.notes: Confirmed both via the City of Tucson's own Residential Solar Permits page (which links to 'TEP Solar Saturation Maps' as a resource) and directly via TEP's own net-metering and residential-interconnection pages, which describe TEP as the interconnecting utility for solar projects within its service territory including Tucson.

value.name: Tucson Electric Power (TEP)
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Arizona this session (Arizona has no CCA framework). Per the Arizona Corporation Commission's October 2018 order, traditional net metering was phased out; new/expanded systems are compensated under TEP's Rider-14 Resource Comparison Proxy (RCP) Export Rate, a buyback rate reset annually and expected to decline roughly 10%/year until it approaches utility-scale solar cost. Customers with pre-existing systems keep traditional net metering (Rider-4, NM-PRS) for 20 years from interconnection. RCP-rate customers must also take service under a Time-of-Use or Demand Time-of-Use pricing plan.

value.name: Arizona Credit for Solar Energy Devices
value.description: Statewide Arizona individual income tax credit under A.R.S. §43-1083: 25% of the cost of installing a solar energy device at the taxpayer's Arizona residence, capped at $1,000 total per residence (not per year — the $1,000 cap is cumulative across all tax years for the same residence). Any unused credit may be carried forward up to 5 consecutive tax years. Applies statewide to any qualifying Arizona residential installation, not utility- or city-specific.
value.eligibility: Arizona resident, not a dependent of another taxpayer, installing a solar energy device (as defined in A.R.S. §42-5001) at their Arizona residence; claimed via Arizona Form 310.
